fiji.overview: Fiji is home to world-class reef breaks like Cloudbreak and Restaurants, drawing experts for heavy, hollow lefts. These waves break over shallow coral and require a boat ride from the main islands. The prime season runs from April to October when powerful swells arrive from the south. It is strictly for experienced surfers, with 77-82 F water and no wetsuit needed.

borabora.overview: French Polynesia is famous for Teahupo'o on Tahiti's southeast coast, a world-class, heavy left-hand reef break strictly for experts. Most breaks here are shallow, razor-sharp reefs requiring a boat to access. The prime season runs from May to September when powerful south swells hit. While experts chase massive barrels, beginners have very few options, limited to a couple of beach breaks like Papara. The water is warm enough to surf without a wetsuit year-round.

months.6: Peak season for south and southwest swells. Teahupo'o fires with world-class, heavy left-hand barrels that can reach 10-15 ft on big days. This is strictly expert territory over a dangerous, shallow reef accessed by boat. The water is 79-81 F, so no wetsuit is needed.

months.6: Peak dry season brings world-class waves to the Bukit Peninsula. Uluwatu and Padang Padang produce heavy, hollow lefts over shallow reef for experts only, often reaching 6-10 ft. Offshore winds groom the waves perfectly. Beginners have smaller, manageable waves at Kuta.

months.1: Winter north swells are at their peak, producing world-class waves. Honolua Bay fires with long, hollow right-handers for experts, and Pe'ahi (Jaws) can see massive 20-foot-plus faces. Intermediate surfers can find smaller days at Ho'okipa, but the north shore is generally for advanced riders.
Peak winter swell from the northeast brings consistent 3-5 ft waves to the east coast beach breaks, suited for intermediate surfers. The water is 49 F, 5/4 mm wetsuit.
months.2: Winter swells ease, offering 2-4 ft waves that suit both brave beginners and intermediates. The water is 47 F.
months.11: Autumn storms give way to the winter northeast swell, bringing consistent 3-5 ft waves to the east coast beach breaks, suited for intermediate surfers. The water is 60 F, 4/3 mm wetsuit.
months.12: Peak winter swell from the northeast brings consistent 3-5 ft waves to the east coast beach breaks, suited for intermediate surfers. The water is 55 F, 5/4 mm wetsuit.
